They're not throttling. People who say so have no idea what that term means. Throttling is cutting your connection speed when certain services are detected. T-Mobile doesn't do this. They intercept the request, and request a standard definition video feed, and then they let you stream for free, all at full speed. The only thing they messed up on was including YouTube without their permission so people couldn't stream videos in HD.
It's not throttling per se, but it's definitely violating net neutrality. I pay for X mbps and up to Y GB/month, not "X mbps on partner sites otherwise Z mbps".

Seeing as how T-Mobile is a mobile carrier, we actually don't pay them for certain mbps. On my plan I get 10g of data/month, not promised any speeds. I appreciate their binge plan because when I am away from my home wifi I can watch videos and stream music without using my 10g. Not sure why people get upset with T-Mobile trying to save them data. Lol. I now watch videos while I'm out when I didn't used to, so I could save data. More watching isn't a bad thing.

I would generally agree with you. The difference here is that:

1) The user has the ability to turn off the feature and view everything in high definition 2) These aren't "partner sites", as Binge-on doesn't require content providers to pay TMobile to participate, only that they reduce the quality of their streams to reduce data usage, and in return, users don't pay for data from these content providers.

By definition "so people couldn't stream videos in HD" is throttling.

noun 1. a device controlling the flow of fuel or power to an engine. "the engines were at full throttle"

By the very definition of the word, the ability of T-Mobile to not allow video to stream at HD, would be controlling the flow of fuel, in this case speed of traffic, to an engine, ie your browser. Optimize has a totallly different meaning than what they are stating as optimize is "rearrange or rewrite (data, software, etc.) to improve efficiency of retrieval or processing" and LOSING the ability to stream in HD would not be IMPROVING anything other than their bottom line. This is clear cut throttling, and all the pathetic attempts to dynamically rename it to sound like something else is just that, pathetic.

TMobile doesn't control the "flow of fuel", as they deliver all data at very fast speeds. What they do is request that Google only pass on the SD quality streams. If you want to use the fuel analogy, its more akin to providing a high speed fuel pump but only squeezing the handle halfway. The speed is there, and available, but its not being used. Moreover, the user always has the ability to turn off the "Binge-on" option and stream at high definition while using their data.

Doesn't youtube use two ways to judge the quality, #1. User preference within the html5 viewer and #2. Speed of connection? So either TMobile is changing your packets to youtube, or they are throttling your bandwidth, there is no "request SD streams" as Google has not signed up for anything or provided them any apis to do so.

Daily Devotional

December 30

13 Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness. 14 Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless. - 2 Peter 3:13-14 (KJV)

 There are several other scriptures telling us that there will be a new heaven and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17, 66:22 & Revelation 21:1) at the end of time. If you want more information about the end of the age, when God pours out His wrath on this present earth, and gives final judgment, see “New Revelations” page on our web site. On the new earth, God will live with mankind (Revelation 21:3), and Jesus will rule, and all us saints will get to live with them forever – praise God. This is when the lamb will lay with the lion and righteousness will rule, and there will no longer be any pain, sickness, death, or tears ever again – Wow!

 Those of us, who are born again, have these things to look forward to, and Peter is telling us that we need to be sure and be found in peace, without spot, and blameless. That does not mean that we will ever be totally sinless, but we can be trying to be as holy as possible (1 Peter 1:15) and that will make us blameless in the sight of God. It takes diligence to be blameless, as you can’t just wish for it, but you must pursue it in everything you say and do. To be right with God, we must try hard to follow all the commands that Jesus gave us, and follow the leading of the Holy Spirit in our lives. Disobeying the Holy Spirit is blasphemy against Him, and can send a born again believer to hell (Matthew 12:31-32). Also you must obey Jesus to assure your salvation (Hebrews 5:9). See our web page for more information on this. Praise God for all His wonderful promises to us, His children – Thank you Lord.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
